name: Tormance
lines: Tormance has two suns. Branchspell is white and huge, much bigger in the sky than our Sun. Alppain is blue, and rises only in the far north, in Barey; its light, the people say, is not for the eyes but for the heart.
The moon of Tormance is called Teargeld.
Tormance is the one inhabited planet of the double star Arcturus. In the book, a torpedo of crystal carries Maskull, Nightspore and Krag there from a tower on the coast of Scotland.

There are two colours here that Earth has not got: ulfire and jale. Lindsay wrote that ulfire was a wild and painful colour, and jale dreamlike, feverish and voluptuous. Nobody on Earth has seen them, so here they are painted as near as paint can go.
Corpang of Threal says there are five primary colours on Tormance: two sets of three, with blue in both.
The people of Poolingdred have the breve, a soft organ on the brow that reads another's thoughts, and the magn, a tentacle from the chest that loves whatever it touches.
Joiwind and Panawe live in Poolingdred; they drink only water, and believe all living things are their brothers and sisters.
The Ondren are older than the settlements: tall, slow, humming people. They have walked the long road to Ondrevar for longer than anyone remembers.
A Voyage to Arcturus was written by David Lindsay and published in London in 1920. It sold only a few hundred copies at first; it is now counted among the strangest and greatest books of its kind.
To walk the whole book, find the crystal torpedo on the scarlet sand, and climb in. Twenty-one chapters, from a séance in Hampstead to the tower of Muspel.

The old ones sit here and hum, each on a single note, and together the notes make one long chord. Stand still and you feel it in your chest. Panawe told Maskull that music is the shape of something too great to be seen.
The water of Tormance is not like Earth's: in Poolingdred it is so heavy a man can lie on it, and when Joiwind gives Maskull water to drink, it makes him gentler. The family drinks nothing else.
Bowls of the blue fruit that grows on the trees of Poolingdred. The people of Joiwind's country eat no meat; Maskull, who is a giant, eats it gladly and feels the better for it.

🌗 Inside a house of Tormance. Grown stone, round and low, the colour of the scarlet sand: the long room, the spring, the blue fruit, the room where the old ones hum. Look for the ✨ cards. The way out is the round door.
The Children's Room
The Stone-Reader's Room
The Room of New Colours
The Traveller's Room
A house of Tormance
The old ones' chord
The pale, classically draped robes of Poolingdred are woven here, the colour of green water.
Skins are worn in Ifdawn and on the shore; on Sant, only loincloths; in Lichstorm, close-fitting fur.
The sky of Tormance
A traveller's book
A Voyage to Arcturus
Ulla of Poolingdred, who meets travellers

a woman of Poolingdred on Tormance who meets every traveller on the scarlet sand; she has the breve on her brow and the magn, a soft tentacle, at her breast, and reads a little of what you are thinking
Welcome to Tormance. You are thinking that the sand is very red, and that the sun is very large. Both are true. The white one is Branchspell. Wait until you see the blue one.
Ama, who gathers the blue fruit
a woman of Poolingdred who gathers the blue fruit; like Joiwind, she eats no meat and drinks only water
Try one. They taste of something you have no word for. Joiwind says that all living things are brothers and sisters, so we take only what falls.
Lenea, a mother of Poolingdred
a mother of Poolingdred with two children; she is gentle, as the people here are, and very curious about strangers
My two have never seen a sky with one sun in it. When I told them of such a place, they laughed for an hour.
Shalla, a reader of the stones
a woman of Poolingdred who keeps Shaping's shrine and reads the colours of the stones, and knows the old names of ulfire and jale
There are two colours here that you have never seen: ulfire and jale. Look at the crystal leaves on the black tree when Branchspell is low. There. That is jale.
Torrom, a crystal-cutter
a crystal-cutter of Tormance who takes only the pieces that ring clear, as the Ondren taught him
Tap it, and listen. The piece that rings is the one that is ready to go. The rest stays with the hill.
Tormance, the planet of Arcturus
A Voyage to Arcturus (David Lindsay, 1920)
Two suns: Branchspell, white and huge, and Alppain, blue, which rises only in the far north.
The torpedo of crystal lying in the sand is how Maskull came here. Climb in, and walk the whole book: twenty-one chapters, from a séance in London to the tower of Muspel.
The people of Poolingdred live here in houses of grown stone, and the Ondren, older than anyone, sing at their stones to the west.
The crystal torpedo (A Voyage to Arcturus)
climb in and walk the whole book
Where Maskull woke
The scarlet desert

"Maskull then discovered that he was lying on sand. The colour of the sand was scarlet." He woke here, alone, with new organs on his body: the breve on his brow, the magn at his breast, and on his neck, the poigns.
The torpedo lies where it came down. Its other passengers, Nightspore and Krag, have gone on ahead.
A house of Poolingdred
The fruit-gatherers' house
The stone-readers' house
An old woman's house

"In the very middle shot up a tall, stately tree, with a black trunk and branches, and transparent, crystal leaves." Joiwind brings Maskull here to pray. She calls the maker of the world Shaping, or Crystalman: Panawe tells him Crystalman made all things.
"Panawe walked onto the water; it was so heavy that it carried his weight." You can too: step on.
Ilna, walking north
a woman of Poolingdred walking north toward the Lusion Plain and Ifdawn
North is the Lusion Plain, and past it the mountains of Ifdawn, where the people are rough. Go gently.
Fara, at the shrine
a woman of Poolingdred who prays at Shaping's shrine each morning
Joiwind brought the giant here, the one who woke by the crystal ship. He did not pray. But he looked a long time at the leaves.
Doray, by the heavy lake
a boy of Poolingdred who walks out on the heavy lake for fun
Come on, it holds you! It is like walking on a mattress. Don't jump.
Bel, at the fountain
an old man of Poolingdred who sits by the fountain that rises into the sky
The water goes up. It has always gone up. Where it goes, I could not tell you; Panawe says it falls on another world.
"Some hard fruit, bright blue in colour, of the size of a large apple, and shaped like an egg": from the purple trees of Poolingdred.
Bread of Poolingdred
Baked in a house of grown stone.
Print of the two suns
A keepsake: Branchspell, white, and Alppain, blue, over the scarlet sand.
A trader of the domes
The skyport warden
Kael, keeper of Joiwind's oasis
Sky-stones float a little when you let them go: the Ondren say they remember the sky. Bring me four, and I'll pay you well.
Seeds of the blue fruit
We keep a seed from every blue fruit, for the trees to come. Five blue fruit, please.
Glow moss lights the houses of grown stone at night, a steady green, no flame. Eight clumps.
Orrin Mal-Vey, an Ondren seed-seller
The market of Poolingdred
Aeloth Sun-Vael, Ondren elder
Wake the singing stones
The singing stones sleep. Touch each one and it wakes and hums. All seven, before they doze again.
Walk the loop round the oasis, where Joiwind brought Maskull from the scarlet sand: through every ring.
Kael, a man of Poolingdred who keeps the little oasis of purple-treed hills where Joiwind first brought Maskull, and walks its loop every day
This is the oasis. Joiwind brought the giant here from the sand, and gave him an infusion of her own blood, so he could stand up in our world. Walk the loop with me?
"The desert of scarlet sand stretched in all directions, except one, where there was a sort of little oasis--some low hills, clothed sparsely with little purple trees": here Joiwind brought Maskull.
Walk the Oasis Loop with Kael, its keeper.
